note: Internal good-practice notes written for this module. They paraphrase common business-plan advice (SBA guide, Business Model Canvas, Lean Canvas pages kept in business_plan/01_plan_structures). They are NOT official BFPME or GIZ requirements and must never be cited as such.

passages.title: Executive summary: write it last, keep it to one page
passages.text: State what the business sells, to whom, why now, how much money is needed and what it will be used for. A reader should know the ask after one page. Repeat only figures that appear later in the plan.

passages.title: Team: show relevant experience and roles
passages.text: For each founder give the role, the relevant experience in years and the gap the team still has. Lenders look for someone who has done something similar and for a named person responsible for finance.

passages.title: Offer: problem, solution, difference
passages.text: Name the customer problem in the customer's words, then the product or service that solves it, then one thing competitors do not offer. Avoid listing features without a customer need.

passages.title: Market: size it with a source
passages.text: Define the target segment, count how many potential customers exist in the area served and cite where the number comes from. Name direct competitors and the main alternative customers use today. Do not use a national market total as if it were your market.

passages.title: Pricing and channels
passages.text: Give the price per unit or plan and say how it was set: cost plus margin, competitor price or willingness to pay. List the channels you will use to reach the first customers and the expected cost of winning one.

passages.title: Operations: equipment, premises, suppliers
passages.text: List the equipment and premises with rent or purchase status. Name main suppliers and say what share of costs is imported or paid in foreign currency because exchange rates affect margins.

passages.title: Human resources: headcount and wages
passages.text: Give headcount per year, average gross salary and the employer social charges used. Check payroll equals headcount times salary times twelve plus charges.

passages.title: Legal form and capital
passages.text: State the legal form, the share capital and who holds what share. If a Startup Act label is planned or held, say so and keep statute questions for the legal assistant rather than quoting rules here.

passages.title: Investment plan: itemise and include working capital
passages.text: List each investment with an amount: equipment, software, fit-out, initial stock, start-up costs and the working capital needed before the first customers pay.

passages.title: Financing plan: sources must equal uses
passages.text: Split funding into own funds, loans and grants. Total sources must equal total uses. If a loan is requested give amount, rate, duration and grace period.

passages.title: Projections: three linked statements
passages.text: Show revenue, direct costs, payroll, other costs, depreciation, interest, tax and net result for each year, a cash plan and the break-even point. Explain what drives revenue growth. Make sure every total is the sum of its lines.

passages.title: Risks: name them and say what you will do
passages.text: List the three to five risks that would hurt most, for example late payment, supplier dependency, currency moves, key-person loss, regulation. For each state one concrete mitigation.

passages.title: Existing activity for an extension
passages.text: Show at least the last two years of revenue and net result, years in operation, main customers and what the extension changes compared with today.

passages.title: Extension: capacity and impact
passages.text: State the added capacity or output, the investment it needs, the expected revenue it brings and the jobs created.

passages.title: Impact
passages.text: Describe jobs created, inclusion of women and young people where relevant, and any environmental effect. Give figures only if you can measure them.
